clue.text: A great number in quite good environs degenerate

indicators.note: 'in ... environs' places the first pieces inside the surrounding word, wrapped round by it
environs are surroundings, so the word they belong to encloses what comes before

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
decent means acceptable, reasonably good

explanation.surface: Lots of people in respectable surroundings have gone to the bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A great number' tempts as one idea; it is A plus a Roman numeral, and D is 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone or something in moral decline, self-indulgent and corrupted.

clue.text: The dyke builder would take endless refuse

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: offal is waste matter, scraps or rubbish

explanation.surface: A man building an embankment would put up with rubbish that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFAL loses its last letter. Offa was the 8th-century king of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke along the English–Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: King Offa is historically credited with constructing the great earthwork named after him, Offa's Dyke.

clue.text: Some are clever, sedulous and learned

indicators.note: 'some' means only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A remark that certain people are bright, diligent and well educated.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across cleVER SEDulous.
explanation.definitionFit: To be versed in a subject is to be knowledgeable or skilled in it, so learned fits as an adjective.

clue.text: Cancel it in error and there'll be a song made!

indicators.note: done in error means done wrongly, so the letters end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Mistakenly call something off and there will be a fuss kicked up about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' lurks behind the surface: making a song about something means fussing over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a hymn or chant, especially one with a biblical text, used in church services.

clue.text: A town in the USA, Princeton say

indicators.note: say signals an example, so the title in front is replaced by a particular holder of it

blocks.note: the first part, prince, is replaced by a famous prince, as 'say' signals
taken as written, the tail of the word

explanation.surface: Princeton offered as an example of an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: Princeton seems the example of the definition, but it splits as Prince + ton, and 'say' asks for an example of a prince. Charleston is a city in South Carolina.
explanation.definitionFit: Charleston is a real city in South Carolina, and another in West Virginia, so it is indeed an American town.

clue.text: A large property - note the extent

blocks.note: G is a note of the musical scale
range means extent or scope

explanation.surface: An estate agent's line about a big house, drawing attention to how far its land stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings attached, typically a substantial estate home.

clue.text: Seed's fan prepared to make a personal complaint

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A gardening enthusiast has been set up to lodge a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance, but here it means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be a bodily ailment or disorder, and loss of hearing is one affecting an individual.

clue.text: High-minded person allowed the last word? That's a bit of a bloomer

blocks.note: ST abbreviates saint, a person of lofty virtue
amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A lofty thinker who gets the final say makes a bit of a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a gaffe, but it is a flower, and the answer is part of one.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing male organ of a flower, so a component of something that blooms.

clue.text: Notice present and hold on

blocks.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
present, as in attendance, means here

explanation.surface: An instruction to observe the gift and keep a grip on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast or cling, which is what holding on means physically.

clue.text: Laughing at a depressed fence?

blocks.note: first meaning: the sound of laughter
second meaning: a boundary wall sunk in a ditch

explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken fence or wall in a ditch, common on English country estates, keeping livestock out without spoiling the view. 'Depressed' means sunk, not gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word represents laughter, and is also the name of a boundary set below ground level in a trench.

clue.text: Inform about a mad character going to pieces

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
the Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Someone grassing on a lunatic who is cracking up.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is underworld slang for informing to the police; the mad character is from Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattering is breaking into fragments, and going to pieces is the same idea, literal or emotional.

clue.text: Retiring artist getting just deserts

definitions.note: a plural-looking idiom used for a single deserved return

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the word is read in the backward direction

blocks.note: a drawer is one who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: A shy painter receives what they have earned.
explanation.definitionFit: Just deserts are what someone deserves, good or bad, so a recompense that matches the merit.

clue.text: Regal resignation

blocks.note: surface reading: a stately, dignified acceptance of fate
setter's reading: a monarch giving up the throne

explanation.walkthrough: Resignation reads as stoic acceptance; here it is literally stepping down, by a king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: When a sovereign formally renounces the throne, that act is the royal form of quitting office.

clue.text: Was more than once granted around a quarter

indicators.note: around means going round, so one piece is wrapped about another

blocks.note: ex means former, once
ceded means handed over, conceded
E, east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Something was more than once allowed in a certain district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than once' looks like a phrase, but the definition ends at 'than'. A quarter is a compass point here.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed is to go beyond a limit or amount, so the past tense means outstripped or surpassed it.

clue.text: A royal house built in Stroud

indicators.note: built means constructed, so the letters are put together in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of this Gloucestershire town are the fodder

explanation.surface: A palace for a king constructed in the Gloucestershire town of Stroud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests a building, but it means a dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the dynasty ruling England from 1485 to 1603, and a royal house is a ruling family.

clue.text: Embarrassed about a misshapen nose, it's thought

definitions.note: a clause; the answer is the adjective meaning thought out

indicators.note: misshapen means badly formed, so the letters are put out of shape
about means around, so one piece surrounds the rest

blocks.note: red-faced with embarrassment
taken as written
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is thought to be ashamed of their crooked nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's thought' stands for the adjective: an argument that is reasoned has been thought out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reasoned has been worked out logically, which is to say properly considered with care.

clue.text: Man races to get in drink that's superior

indicators.note: to get in means to enter, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: beer is a drink
the TT, Tourist Trophy, motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Racing on the Isle of Man leads to finer drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, home of the TT motorcycle races, not a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Better is the comparative of good, meaning of higher quality or standing, which is what superior means.

clue.text: Involving the bell-boy in strikes could well cause storms

indicators.note: involving means including within, so one word is held inside another

blocks.note: rams means strikes hard, batters
a page is a hotel bell-boy

explanation.surface: Bringing the hotel porter into industrial action may well stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' looks like walkouts; it is the verb for hitting. RAMS holds PAGE: RAM(PAGE)S.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently, and storms as a verb means charging around in a rage.

clue.text: Band having an outing in the Canterbury area

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: Canterbury is in Kent, in the south-east of England
a trip is an outing

explanation.surface: A group of musicians on an excursion around Canterbury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like musicians; it means a strip of colour. SE holds TRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow strip of colour or material, which is one sense of a band.

clue.text: Quiet charm and taste

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
to enchant is to charm

explanation.surface: A list of understated virtues: quiet charm and good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or fondness for something, matching taste in the sense of a preference.

clue.text: The self-centred individual, for example, is to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form anew, so the letters are shaped into a new order

blocks.note: e.g. abbreviates for example
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A selfish person, for instance, is due to mend their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoist puts their own interests first, which is exactly what being self-centred means.

clue.text: A country hat

blocks.note: first meaning: a Central American nation
second meaning: a woven straw hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Country hat' reads as rustic headgear, but splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a nation on the Central American isthmus, and also a lightweight hat plaited from palm straw.

clue.text: An old-fashioned cold remedy some airmen prepare

blocks.note: POs, pilot officers, are some RAF officers
to set is to make ready, prepare

explanation.surface: Members of an air crew make up a traditional cure for a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A posset is a hot drink of milk curdled with ale or wine, once given to people suffering from colds.

clue.text: The defence work in successes with hardly any encouragement

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a fort is a defensive stronghold
wins are successes
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A military post that triumphs when nobody urges it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence work' looks like one fortification, but it splits into two pieces; op, from opus, is a crossword staple for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very readily, needing almost no persuasion, as in 'I'd quit for two pins'.

clue.text: Making tin and silver amalgam presents a problem

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A metallurgist finds that alloying tin with silver causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected obstacle or drawback, which is one kind of difficulty.

clue.text: Gratuities may be used up for a rotisserie

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: tips are gratuities

explanation.surface: Tip money might be spent on a roasting machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is the rotating rod for roasting meat over a fire, which is what a rotisserie is.

clue.text: Breaking a horse? Not in the main

indicators.note: breaking smashes something apart, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Taming a horse is not, for the most part, what happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly'; the main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the open sea, and being on land means being out of it.

clue.text: They're on their own before the children appear

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before
mites are small children

explanation.surface: People are alone until the kids turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eremites are hermits, religious recluses who live in solitude away from society.
